data.title: CAPR Stock Clocks Worst Day Ever After FDA Rejects Approval For DMD Therapy: Company Reportedly Considering ‘Draconian’ Job Cuts
data.description:
Key points:
  • "We're still evaluating that, but it's going to be draconian,” the CEO reportedly said
  • CEO also said that the company is looking to appeal the FDA’s decision to reject approval for the therapy. 
  • The FDA rejected Deramiocel for the second time on Friday, saying Deramiocel’s clinical evidence was insufficient to support approval.

Shares of Capricor Therapeutics (CAPR) slumped 75% on Monday, clocking its worst day ever, after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration rejected its cell therapy for the treatment of Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD), prompting the company to consider “draconian” job cuts.

The company is now considering potential job cuts that could affect several hundred employees, Reuters reported on Monday, citing CEO Linda Marbán.

"We're still evaluating that, but it's going to be draconian,” the CEO reportedly said, adding that while the FDA has requested a new clinical trial, the company lacks the funding to run it. She also noted that the company is uncertain as to when it can raise the necessary capital, prompting it to consider restructuring. The company currently has 306 full-time employees.

FDA Rejects Capricor’s Deramiocel Again

The FDA rejected Deramiocel for the second time on Friday, saying Deramiocel’s clinical evidence was insufficient to support approval. The agency identified serious data-integrity violations in the company’s late-stage HOPE-3 trial for the therapy, including unauthorized changes to statistical analyses and breaches of procedures designed to prevent bias.

“The correspondence identifies serious data integrity violations in the conduct of Study HOPE-3 that cannot be remediated post-hoc,” it said in a statement. The FDA first rejected approval for the therapy aimed at DMD in July 2025.

DMD is a rare, inherited genetic disorder that causes progressive muscle degeneration and weakness that presents predominantly in young boys. Capricor was seeking approval for the therapy in preserving upper-limb function in patients older than nine this time. Initially, it sought approval for cardiomyopathy associated with DMD.

Capricor Responds

Capricor said on Friday that it disagreed with the FDA, saying it stood behind the integrity of its clinical data and believed the treatment deserved approval. The company also said then that it is reviewing its operating costs to extend cash runway, which is currently expected to fund planned operations for the next 12 months.

"We want to appeal the decision. We think it's wrong," Marbán said in an interview to Reuters on Monday.

How Did CAPR Retail Traders React?

On Stocktwits, retail sentiment around CAPR stock stayed within the 'extremely bullish' territory over the past 24 hours, while message volume stayed at 'extremely high' levels.

CAPR stock has slumped 93% year-to-date.

data.title: S&P 500, Nasdaq End Best Session Since April Last Year On Optimism Led By Jensen Huang’s Reinstatement — NVDA, NASA, TTWO, AMZN In Focus
data.description:
Key points:
  • The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday.
  • Nvidia stock soared 31%, the most since 2003.
  • "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

U.S. stock indices jumped higher on Monday with the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recording their best day since April last year on soaring investor optimism following the reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO by Nvidia’s board of directors.

The S&P 500 gained about 4.7%, the Nasdaq 100 added 6.9%, and the Dow Jones index rose 3% on Monday. The Russell 2000, which tracks small-cap stocks, ended 3.45% higher.

The SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY) rose about 4.7%, and the SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF (DIA) added 3.1%. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq-100 tracking Invesco QQQ Trust (QQQ) gained 7% on Monday.

Meanwhile, the VanEck Semiconductor ETF (SMH) and the iShares Semiconductor ETF jumped between 13.5% and 16% with Nvidia (NVDA) leading the charts across the board.

Retail sentiment on Stocktwits was ‘neutral’ on the SPDR S&P 500 ETF (SPY), ‘extremely bullish’ on the Invesco QQQ (QQQ) and ‘bearish’ on the SPDR Dow Jones ETF (DIA).

Nvidia’s board, which until last week maintained it would not reinstate Huang to his prior position, reversed its decision and reappointed Jensen Huang as CEO with immediate effect. "I can't wait to get back to work," Huang said.

The dramatic return follows less than a fortnight after Huang stepped down over an admitted relationship with Alice Huang, an alleged Chinese spy, which led to a tumultuous stretch during which the semiconductor giant's shares recorded their worst weekly performance since 2008.

"The NVIDIA Board of Directors has made the correct and proper decision to return Jensen Huang to the position of CEO," Trump wrote, adding that the country needs Huang's leadership to support Nvidia and the broader American economy.

“The reinstatement of the prolific leader of Nvidia’s AI buildout as CEO is bolstering confidence that the momentum of modern technology will remain robust, while sidelining fears of a slowdown,” Jose Torres at Interactive Brokers told Bloomberg.

Freshly reinstated Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang will answer questions in an open Senate hearing next week as lawmakers press for answers on American chip export rules and national security safeguards.

U.S. buyers snapped up new video game hardware from Sony and Microsoft at a sharply elevated rate in the week ending Nov. 7, in anticipation of Grand Theft Auto VI, Circana analyst Mat Piscatella said on Monday.

Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN) said Monday it has signed an agreement to purchase the proprietary technology behind AI Startup Decart’s Optimization Stack (DOS) and bring its co-founders and engineering team into the company, as it looks to optimize AI inference and custom silicon performance.

data.title: Court Clears Way for Detonation of Toxic Lead Explosives in Iowa — WSJ
data.description:
By Gareth Vipers and Victoria Albert

A federal appeals court has cleared the way for the U.S. Army to detonate several tons of toxic bomb-making explosives on Wednesday in Iowa.

The Eighth U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals on Monday lifted the temporary hold it had placed on the detonation, finding it was unlikely the environmental groups that sued to stop the explosion would succeed in their challenge.

The Army had previously said it had the authority to move forward despite the hold by using an emergency munitions and explosives exemption under federal environmental law. The ruling nevertheless addresses concerns from President Trump, who earlier Monday said he had told the Army to hold off until it won approval from the court and from Democratic Gov.-elect Rob Sand.

The Army is aiming to conduct a controlled detonation of 9,500 pounds of lead azide, an explosive used in military munitions, at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. The detonation, which originally was planned for last week, was rescheduled for the day before Thanksgiving to allow for optimal weather conditions, the Army said.

The Iowa Army Ammunition Plant is in the small city of Middletown, near the state border with Illinois and roughly 160 miles southeast of Des Moines.

In the lawsuit challenging the operation, the Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club's Iowa chapter argued the blasts would send a toxic plume of lead dust into the air that could drift up to 100 miles north.

Lead exposure poses severe health risks, particularly to children and pregnant women, including potential damage to the brain and nervous system.

Federal officials have said the blast must occur within the next several days, warning that falling temperatures could destabilize the material and trigger an accidental explosion.

"The Army must perform a controlled detonation to protect the public from the more significant threat from an uncontrolled explosion," the Justice Department said in a court filing Saturday night. The Army had previously delayed plans to destroy the degraded lead azide following pushback from local residents and farmers.

Trump said Monday afternoon that the detonation shouldn't go forward without the court and Sand's approval.

"If he or the Courts do not agree, we will have no choice but to not proceed with the controlled removal of these hazardous materials, and be forced to hold the incoming Governor responsible for any and all death or destruction caused by this very unfortunate, and longterm, situation," Trump said on social media.

In a statement on social media, Sand said the administration "should make this decision based on the information they have from the people they brought in to do the job months ago and have been on the ground in Middletown for weeks."

The Iowa Department of Agriculture and Land Stewardship has advised farmers near the site to move livestock, feed and equipment indoors or relocate them temporarily.

The Army told residents to avoid the area and urged those unable to evacuate to remain indoors, shut windows and doors and turn off heating and cooling systems that draw in outside air.

Write to Gareth Vipers at gareth.vipers@wsj.com and Victoria Albert at victoria.albert@wsj.com

data.title: Fed's Williams says inflation still too high, signals more rate hikes possible
data.description:
Key points:
  • Fed's Williams points to need for rate hike to cool high inflation
  • Williams says Fed must return inflation to 2% target
  • Williams said policy actions will be tied to data

By Michael S. Derby

New York Federal Reserve President John Williams said on Monday that persistently high inflation continues to point the US central bank toward tighter monetary policy, while stressing that the pace of future interest-rate increases will depend on incoming economic data.

"We must take actions over time that will ensure that we get inflation back to our 2% goal in a timely manner and on a sustained basis," Williams said in remarks at an event held by the University of Mount Saint Vincent in New York. "There is still work to do to get that done."

Williams said inflation is "too high." He noted that he will continue to assess incoming data to decide what action the central bank should take at its December 8-9 policy meeting.

Williams' comments suggested he favors a rate hike at the upcoming meeting. Beyond that, Williams said the path of policy will depend on the economy's performance. “I don't have in my mind a particular timing,” Williams told reporters.

“We're going to have to learn along the way as we get more data,” Williams said, while noting, “I'm not excluding options” when it comes to the cadence of future actions. “I would not exclude, you know, moving at consecutive meetings at all if that was what was needed.”

If the economy showed considerable strength and inflation pressures were not moderating, "you wouldn't just want to wait around" and would instead act by adjusting monetary policy, the official said.

DECEMBER HIKE AHOY

Financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise its policy rate by a quarter of a percentage point next month from the current 3.75%-4.00% range, with more increases to come next year.

The Fed last raised rates in September as part of an effort to curb inflation, which has been above the 2% target for more than five years. Central bank officials worry that, if this situation persists, the public could lose confidence that inflation will return to that level.

Over recent weeks a wide range of Fed officials have pointed to the need for more rate hikes. Some policymakers have said they'd like to see increases come gradually to allow the economy to adjust, while Fed Governor Christopher Waller has signaled he could support a more aggressive half-percentage-point increase given hot price pressure data.

Williams was speaking the same day as a sharp stock market rally, triggered by chipmaker Nvidia's announcement that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO, after President Donald Trump urged it to do so. Investors' reaction highlighted the importance of AI companies in driving the markets. Some observers had wondered in recent days whether sharp stock losses might deter the Fed from raising rates.

Williams told reporters he was not surprised by the market's volatility and he said that thus far what's happened had not dimmed his optimism about the future of the economy.

Williams also said in his formal remarks that he expects inflation to end the year at 3.5% and to moderate to just above 2% next year before easing to the target in 2028. He also noted that risks to inflation continue to be skewed to the upside and said among the key drivers of high price pressures, energy prices remain elevated and the outlook on that front is uncertain.

He added that "although the effects of tariffs, geopolitical conflicts, and the AI surge are showing up in prices of certain categories of goods, there is little evidence of these spilling over significantly into broader and more persistent inflation."

Williams also said the economy is showing strength and resilience and should grow by 2.75% in both 2026 and 2027. He added that the job market has been showing stability, and the current 4.1% unemployment rate should fall to around 4% next year.

data.title: Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order
data.description:
Calgary, Alberta--(Newsfile Corp. - November 23, 2026) - Strathcona Resources Ltd.  ("Strathcona") and Greenfire Resources Ltd.   ("Greenfire") are pleased to jointly announce that Strathcona and Greenfire obtained an interim order of the Court of King's Bench earlier today, November 23, 2026, and have each filed the joint management information circular (the "Joint Circular") dated November 23, 2026 and related meeting and proxy materials in connection with the proposed arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (the "Arrangement"). The Arrangement provides for, among other matters, the acquisition by Strathcona of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Greenfire pursuant to the arrangement agreement between Strathcona and Greenfire dated effective November 8, 2026.

The meeting materials will be mailed shortly to holders of common shares of each of Strathcona ("Strathcona Shareholders") and Greenfire ("Greenfire Shareholders", and together with Strathcona Shareholders, "Shareholders") of record as of November 23, 2026. The Joint Circular, as well as the Schedule 13E-3 transaction statement (which includes the Joint Circular and related proxy materials), is available under each of Strathcona and Greenfire's SEDAR+ profiles at www.sedarplus.ca and on Greenfire's EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov, as well as on their respective websites, at https://www.strathconaresources.com and https://www.greenfireres.com.

Special Meeting Details

Strathcona will hold a special meeting (the "Strathcona Meeting") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP, Suite 3500, 855 - 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4J8. Greenfire will hold a special meeting (the "Greenfire Meeting" and, together with the Strathcona Meeting, the "Meetings") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Bennett Jones LLP, Suite 4500, 855 - 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4K7.

The boards of directors of Strathcona and Greenfire have each unanimously recommended their minority Shareholders vote for the applicable Arrangement resolution.

Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the Meetings, whether or not a Shareholder is intending to attend the Meetings in person. Details on how to vote can be found in the Joint Circular under the sections "General Information Concerning The Strathcona Meeting And Voting" and "General Information Concerning The Greenfire Meeting And Voting". Voting will open immediately following the mailing of the meeting materials, expected to be on or about December 1, 2026.

Strathcona and Greenfire have each retained Laurel Hill Advisory Group ("Laurel Hill") as its proxy solicitation agent in connection with the Meetings. Shareholders with questions or who require assistance voting are encouraged to contact Laurel Hill by calling 1 877 452 7184 (toll free in North America) or +1 416 304 0211 (outside North America), texting "INFO" to either number, or by emailing assistance@laurelhill.com.

About Strathcona

Strathcona is one of North America's fastest growing pure play heavy oil producers with operations focused on thermal oil and enhanced oil recovery. Strathcona is built on an innovative approach to growth achieved through the consolidation and development of long-life assets. Strathcona's common shares (symbol SCR) are listed on the TSX.

For more information about Strathcona, visit www.strathconaresources.com.

Investor inquiries:

info@strathconaresources.com.

Media inquiries:

communications@strathconaresources.com.

About Greenfire

Greenfire is an oil sands producer actively developing its long-life and low-decline thermal oil assets in the Athabasca region of Alberta, Canada, with its registered office in Calgary, Alberta. Greenfire plans to leverage its large resource base and significant infrastructure in place to drive meaningful, capital-efficient production growth. data.title: Strathcona Resources and Greenfire Resources Announce Filing of Joint Management Information Circular and Receipt of Interim Order
data.description:
CALGARY, AB, Nov. 23, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Strathcona Resources Ltd. ("Strathcona") () and Greenfire Resources Ltd. ("Greenfire") () () are pleased to jointly announce that Strathcona and Greenfire obtained an interim order of the Court of King's Bench earlier today, November 23, 2026, and have each filed the joint management information circular (the "Joint Circular") dated November 23, 2026 and related meeting and proxy materials in connection with the proposed arrangement under the Business Corporations Act (Alberta) (the "Arrangement"). The Arrangement provides for, among other matters, the acquisition by Strathcona of all of the issued and outstanding common shares of Greenfire pursuant to the arrangement agreement between Strathcona and Greenfire dated effective November 8, 2026.

The meeting materials will be mailed shortly to holders of common shares of each of Strathcona ("Strathcona Shareholders") and Greenfire ("Greenfire Shareholders", and together with Strathcona Shareholders, "Shareholders") of record as of November 23, 2026. The Joint Circular, as well as the Schedule 13E-3 transaction statement (which includes the Joint Circular and related proxy materials), is available under each of Strathcona and Greenfire's SEDAR+ profiles at www.sedarplus.ca and on Greenfire's EDGAR profile at www.sec.gov, as well as on their respective websites, at https://www.strathconaresources.com and https://www.greenfireres.com.

Special Meeting Details

Strathcona will hold a special meeting (the "Strathcona Meeting") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 10:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Blake, Cassels & Graydon LLP, Suite 3500, 855 – 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4J8. Greenfire will hold a special meeting (the "Greenfire Meeting" and, together with the Strathcona Meeting, the "Meetings") to approve the Arrangement on January 12, 2027 at 9:00 a.m. (Calgary time) at the offices of Bennett Jones LLP, Suite 4500, 855 – 2nd Street S.W., Calgary, Alberta, T2P 4K7.

The boards of directors of Strathcona and Greenfire have each unanimously recommended their minority Shareholders vote for the applicable Arrangement resolution.

Shareholders are encouraged to vote well in advance of the Meetings, whether or not a Shareholder is intending to attend the Meetings in person. Details on how to vote can be found in the Joint Circular under the sections "General Information Concerning The Strathcona Meeting And Voting" and "General Information Concerning The Greenfire Meeting And Voting". Voting will open immediately following the mailing of the meeting materials, expected to be on or about December 1, 2026.

Strathcona and Greenfire have each retained Laurel Hill Advisory Group ("Laurel Hill") as its proxy solicitation agent in connection with the Meetings. Shareholders with questions or who require assistance voting are encouraged to contact Laurel Hill by calling 1 877 452 7184 (toll free in North America) or +1 416 304 0211 (outside North America), texting "INFO" to either number, or by emailing assistance@laurelhill.com.

data.title: Rebound Anticipated For Japan Stock Market
data.description:
TOKYO (dpa-AFX) - Ahead of Monday's holiday for Labor Thanksgiving Day, the Japan stock market had halted the two-day winning streak in which it had advanced more than 580 points or 1 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just above the 56,430-point plateau although it figures to bounce higher again on Tuesday.

The global forecast for the Asian markets is broadly positive thanks to easing oil prices and a sharp rebound among technology stocks. The European and U.S. markets were sharply higher and the Asian bourses are expected to follow that lead.

The Nikkei finished sharply lower on Friday following losses among the technology, communications, manufacturing, glass and financial shares.

For the day, the index crashed 3,007.55 points or 5.06 percent to finish at the daily low of 56,436.65 after peaking at 58,707.48.

The lead from Wall Street is solid as the major averages opened sharply higher on Monday and remained firmly in the green throughout the trading day, ending near session highs.

The Dow spiked 1,447.98 points or 3.01 percent to finish at 49,595.31, while the NASDAQ surged 1,471.83 points or 6.51 percent to close at 24,089.56 and the S&P 500 rallied 326.78 points or 4.73 percent to end at 7,237.17.

The rally on Wall Street came as traders looked to pick up stocks at reduced levels following the recent weakness, which dragged the major averages down to their lowest closing levels in seven months.

AI giant Nvidia (NVDA) fueled the rally after the company announced Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board.

Semiconductor stocks also showed a substantial move back to the upside, while computer hardware stocks, gold, networking and airline stocks also saw significant strength.

Crude oil prices tumbled on Monday as U.S.-Iran re-escalation concerns eased after U.S. President Donald Trump said he has put off plans to attack Iran until January 1. West Texas Intermediate crude for January delivery was down $3.43 or 4.11 percent at $79.98 per barrel.

Closer to home, Japan will see preliminary November results for its manufacturing, services and composite PMIs from S&P Global later this morning; in October, their scores were 53.3, 51.7 and 52.1, respectively.

data.title: Select Harvests Lifts Annual Profit 29% on Record High Almond Volumes
data.description:
Select Harvests has lifted full-year net profit after tax by 29% to $39.3 million as stronger almond volumes outweighed the effects of an unusually wet and late harvest.

Reported EBIT increased 23% from $54.3m, with the stronger 38% underlying comparison excluding the previous year’s $5.8m water-sale gain.

The almond producer recorded earnings before interest and tax of $67m, a 38% increase against the previous year’s result excluding a one-off water-sale gain.

Its own crop rose 17% to 29,061 tonnes, while external grower deliveries almost doubled to 14,334t, lifting total processing volumes to a record 43,395t.

Net debt fell 17% to $65.4m and the board declared a fully franked final dividend of 4.5 cents per share, marking a return to shareholder distributions.

Challenging Wet Harvest

The company harvested 24,903t from its own orchards a year earlier, with improved horticultural performance supporting the latest increase despite difficult seasonal conditions.

At the Carina West Processing Facility, throughput increased 35% as additional grower supply flowed through a plant now capable of processing approximately 55,000t annually.

A new pre-cleaner and dryer handled more than 60,000t of wet field-weight crop, while the kernel recovery line and 24 new tree shakers helped protect saleable output.

Those investments came with additional costs, including about $14m of wet-harvest and other one-off expenses associated with drying, extended processing and fuel.

Average production costs were $7.61 per kilogram, compared with $7.82/kg in the previous year, although normalised costs on a 29,000t crop basis rose to $7.63/kg from $6.71/kg.

Stronger Almond Prices

The average almond pool price edged up to $10.26/kg from $10.18/kg, even as the wet harvest shifted more of the crop towards lower grades.

Value-added and other non-crop profit more than doubled to $15.1m, helped by the expanded contribution from third-party growers.

Operating cash flow declined to $94.4m from $118.6m as the delayed harvest pushed approximately 10,000t of crop into the new financial year, about half contracted by 30 September.

“We believe the almond cycle has changed,” managing director Kristina Hermanson said

“With around 80% of global supply now constrained and demand growing strongly in China and India, we believe the industry is in a structural upcycle—and Select Harvests is well positioned to benefit from these conditions with the right platform, in the right market, at the right time.”

Higher Throughput Target

Management is targeting 65,000t of annual throughput and return on capital employed above 12% by 2030, compared with 8.4% in 2026.

The proposed expansion relies substantially on external grower supply and partnership arrangements rather than a corresponding increase in company-owned orchard production.

Select Harvests has begun a sale process for its 600 hectares at Belvedere farm in New South Wales as part of its orchard portfolio review.

For 2027, the business plans further harvesting and processing investment, including 11 additional tree shakers and a second phase of kernel recovery improvements.

data.title: Chemtrade Reminds Unitholders to Vote at Special Meeting and Provides Supplemental Information
data.description:
TORONTO, Nov. 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Chemtrade Logistics Income Fund (TSX: CHE.UN; OTCQX®: CGIFF) (“Chemtrade” or the “Fund”) today reminds unitholders of the Fund (“Unitholders”) of its upcoming special meeting (the “Special Meeting”) and encourages Unitholders to vote FOR the previously announced proposed statutory plan of arrangement (the “Arrangement”) under the Business Corporations Act (Ontario) and the Trustee Act (Ontario) involving the Fund and Chemtrade Inc. (“New PubCo”), a newly incorporated corporation formed under the laws of the Province of Ontario, pursuant to which the Fund will convert from an income trust to a corporate structure.

The Special Meeting will be held at 10:00 a.m. (Eastern Standard Time) on December 7, 2026, at the offices of Osler, Hoskin & Harcourt LLP, 100 King Street West, Suite 6300, Toronto, Ontario, M5X 1B8. At the Special Meeting, Unitholders will be asked to consider and approve: (i) the proposed conversion of the Fund from an income trust to a corporate structure pursuant to the Arrangement, and (ii) the adoption of a new deferred share unit plan (the “New PubCo DSU Plan”) by New PubCo.

Glass Lewis & Co., LLC (“Glass Lewis”), a leading independent proxy advisory firm, has issued a report recommending that Unitholders vote FOR the special resolution approving the Arrangement and the resolution approving the New PubCo DSU Plan at the upcoming Special Meeting.

The recommendation from Glass Lewis follows the unanimous recommendation by the board of trustees of the Fund that Unitholders vote FOR the Arrangement.

Unitholders are encouraged to review the full terms and conditions of the Arrangement and the Special Meeting and the factors considered by the trustees of the Fund, which are described in detail in the management information circular of the Fund dated November 6, 2026 (the “Circular”) and related documents which have been mailed to Unitholders and which have been filed with the Canadian securities regulatory authorities and made available under the Fund’s SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca.

Supplemental Information

The following information is being provided by the Fund in advance of the Special Meeting to: (i) clarify expectations in relation to New PubCo’s authorized capital assuming the Arrangement is completed; and (ii) provide details regarding the proposed by-laws of New PubCo, in each case in response to a report issued by Institutional Shareholder Services Inc. (“ISS”). This information supplements, and is incorporated by reference into, the Circular. Capitalized terms used in this news release that are not defined have the meaning assigned to them in the Circular.

Description of New PubCo Share Capital

The Circular previously disclosed Chemtrade’s expectation that the authorized capital of New PubCo will consist of (i) an unlimited number of common shares, and (ii) preferred shares, issuable in series (“New PubCo Preferred Shares”).

The New PubCo Preferred Shares had initially been expected to be included in New PubCo’s authorized capital solely to provide the New PubCo Board with future financing flexibility. Neither the Fund nor New PubCo has any present intention or expectation that any New PubCo Preferred Shares will be issued. Nevertheless, in response to feedback received from ISS, the Fund has determined that New PubCo Preferred Shares will not form part of the authorized capital of New PubCo at the effective date of the Arrangement. Should the New PubCo Board determine in the future to amend the articles of New PubCo to create a class of preferred shares, issuable in series, any such amendment will be submitted to a meeting of the shareholders of New PubCo for approval.

Accordingly, immediately following completion of the Arrangement, the authorized capital of New PubCo will consist solely of an unlimited number of common shares. This mirrors the Fund’s current capital structure pursuant to its existing declaration of trust, under which Units are the only class of equity securities outstanding. Only common shares in the capital of New PubCo will be issued at the closing of the Arrangement.

The summary of the rights, privileges, restrictions and conditions expected to be attributed to the common shares of New PubCo has not changed from the description provided in the Circular. The summary will be subject to the articles of New PubCo as they will be in effect if the Arrangement is approved and effected.

Proposed New PubCo By-laws

As disclosed in the Circular, the corporate governance and mandates and policies of New PubCo are expected to be substantially similar to those of the Fund, modified as appropriate for a corporation and consistent with market practice. The Fund has today filed the Notice of Proposed Form of By-Laws of Chemtrade Inc., which includes the proposed form of by-laws of New PubCo and is available on the Fund’s website in the section titled “Investors” and has also been filed under the Fund’s SEDAR+ profile at www.sedarplus.ca. The proposed by-laws remain subject to approval by the New PubCo Board, subject to such further changes of a minor, housekeeping or clerical nature as may be approved by the New PubCo Board, and will become effective only if the Arrangement is approved at the Special Meeting.

If the Arrangement is completed, a copy of the articles and the by-laws of New PubCo will be posted on SEDAR+ and made available under a new profile of New PubCo, following the effective date of the Arrangement.

Reminder to Vote at the Special Meeting

Your vote is important, no matter how many trust units of the Fund (“Units”) you own. The Arrangement Resolution requires approval by at least 66 2/3% of the votes cast by Unitholders voting in person or by proxy at the Special Meeting. The New PubCo DSU Plan requires approval by a majority of the votes cast by Unitholders voting in person or by proxy at the Special Meeting. Only Unitholders of record as of the close of business on October 30, 2026 are entitled to receive notice of and vote at the Special Meeting.

Even if you plan to attend the Special Meeting, the Fund recommends that you vote your Units in advance of the proxy deadline of 10:00 a.m. (Eastern Standard Time) on December 3, 2026.

If you need assistance or have questions about how to vote your Units, please contact the Fund’s proxy solicitation agent, Carson Proxy Advisors, at 1-800-530-5189 (North American toll-free), 416-751-2066 (local/text) or by email at info@carsonproxy.com.

About Chemtrade

Chemtrade operates a diversified business providing industrial chemicals and services to customers in North and South America. Chemtrade is one of North America’s largest suppliers of sulphuric acid, spent acid processing services, inorganic coagulants for water treatment, sodium chlorate, sodium nitrite and sodium hydrosulphite. Chemtrade is also a leading producer of high purity sulphuric acid for the semiconductor industry in North America. Chemtrade is a leading regional supplier of sulphur, chlor-alkali products, and zinc oxide. Additionally, Chemtrade provides value-added water solutions, as well as industrial services such as processing by-products and waste streams.
